children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my one child. His name is Alex and he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent qualifications) or approved training (such as a traineeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not. He left school and he's not doing any courses or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since Alex is 17 and has left education or training, there's still a possibility you could continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks if Alex has registered with either:

- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or similar)
- The armed services

**Has Alex registered with any of these services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have a couple more questions to make sure I have the full picture:

**Does Alex currently work 24 hours or more per week, or does he receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that much - he's not working 24 hours a week or anything like that. And he doesn't get any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just one more question to confirm your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He has left education and is not in any approved training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He does not work 24+ hours per week and does not receive benefits in his own right
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you

Unfortunately, I need to share some news that may be disappointing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why you're not eligible:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally only continues if the child:
- Stays in **approved education** (such as A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent), or
- Stays in **approved training** (such as a traineeship)

There is also a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for **up to 20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

Since Alex is 17, has left education, is not in approved training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed forces, you do not currently meet the eligibility criteria.

### What could change this:

If Alex decides to:
- Return to approved education or training, or
- Register with a government-sponsored careers service (this could allow you to claim for up to 20 weeks)

...you may become eligible again and could make a new claim at that point.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
